audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-centric specifications (P2P networking eth/70, SSTORE gas metering, access list transactions, Prague gas mechanics, bloom filters, DAO fork, Gray Glacier difficulty, GraphQL API, private key encapsulation) and CL-adjacent SSZ merkleization (EIP-7916). The majority is EL logic with one CL serialization spec.

in_scope: P2P Networking (eth/70 handshake, block range queries)
Gas Mechanics (Prague fork: memory, storage, blob, call gas)
Merkle Proof Generation for Light Clients

el_vectors.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_sendRawTransaction, eth_getLogs) and GraphQL API (/graphql port 8547)
el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, oversized access lists for gas exhaustion, crafted SSTORE patterns to exploit gas refund mechanics, DoS via expensive GraphQL queries, log filter abuse via bloom filter false positives
False block range advertisements to disrupt sync, Sybil attacks with coordinated false range claims, invalid block propagation, eclipse attacks

cl_vectors.threat: Craft malicious SSZ data to exploit progressive merkleization, provide invalid proofs to light clients

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/70 P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth/70 Status handshake, RequestBlockRange (0x0b), SendBlockRange (0x0c)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Block range claims are unverified until blocks are actually fetched. Peers can advertise false ranges to waste resources or disrupt sync.

trusted_external_entities.name: Coordinated Malicious Peers via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth/70 Status handshake with false blockRange
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Multiple attacker-controlled nodes can coordinate false block range advertisements. No authentication on P2P; Sybil attacks are feasible.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_sendRawTransaction RPC (Type 0, Type 1 access list transactions)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via public RPC. No authentication required. Transactions may contain oversized access lists, crafted SSTORE patterns, or malformed RLP.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P Transaction Relay
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers relay transactions over unauthenticated P2P network. Transaction bytes may be malformed or malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client via eth_getLogs / Bloom Query
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_getLogs JSON-RPC, bloom filter log queries
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External clients query logs via RPC. Queries are unauthenticated and may craft expensive filter patterns to exhaust node resources.

trusted_external_entities.name: Client via GraphQL API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: GraphQL /graphql endpoint (port 8547), queries and sendRawTransaction mutation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: GraphQL API is unauthenticated by default. No rate limiting specified in EIP-1767. Expensive queries possible. Mutation allows transaction submission.

trusted_external_entities.name: PoW Miner via P2P Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p block propagation (blocks with difficulty, extraData)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners produce blocks propagated via unauthenticated P2P. Blocks may have incorrect difficulty calculation or missing DAO fork extraData. PoW and difficulty must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Block Relay
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blocks received from P2P network are untrusted. Difficulty, PoW, state root, and all header fields must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: DAO Token Holder via Contract Call
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any address can call the recovery contract. Balance verification against mainDAO token is required before any transfer.

trusted_external_entities.name: Sender Application via Key Encapsulation Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Sender provides private key and recipient public key. The public key's authenticity must be verified via signature/trust chain. Transport channel is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Recipient Application via Key Encapsulation Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Recipient generates ephemeral keys and provides public key to sender. If signature verification is skipped, MITM is possible. Ephemeral keys must use CSRNG.

trusted_external_entities.name: Key Provider via Untrusted Channel
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EIP-6051 public key transmission with optional signature
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public keys may be transmitted over untrusted channels. Without signature verification, attacker can substitute their own public key (MITM). Trust chain validation is optional.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client / Proof Verifier
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External verifiers request proofs for list elements. Requests are unauthenticated. Malicious indices or oversized lists could be used for resource exhaustion.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block range claims in Status message must not be trusted. Node must verify claimed ranges by actually requesting blocks. Dishonest peers must be detected and marked unreliable.
Updated block range claims must be verified through actual block retrieval. Peers advertising false ranges should be penalized and disconnected.
Node must maintain diversity in peer connections and not rely solely on block range advertisements for sync decisions. Coordinated false advertisements must not prevent block discovery.

Full transaction validation required: RLP decoding, signature verification, chain ID check, access list format validation (20-byte addresses, 32-byte keys), intrinsic gas calculation including access list costs (2400/address + 1900/key). Oversized access lists bounded by block gas limit.
Identical validation as RPC-submitted transactions. Transaction type byte, RLP structure, field count, access list structure, and signature must all be validated before mempool admission.

Log queries must be bounded to prevent resource exhaustion. Bloom filter pre-filtering provides efficiency but false positives require full log verification. Address and topic filters must be validated.

GraphQL queries must be validated against schema. Input scalar types (Bytes32, Address, Bytes, BigInt) must be format-validated. Signing, compiling, and mining operations must be denied. Rate limiting and access control must be implemented at deployment level. Deeply nested or expensive queries must be bounded.
RLP-encoded transaction must be fully validated (same as eth_sendRawTransaction). Only sendRawTransaction mutation is allowed; no signing or account management operations exposed.

Block difficulty must be recomputed using Gray Glacier formula (11.4M block delay) and verified against header. PoW must be verified via ethash. Blocks in range 1920000-1920009 must contain 'dao-hard-fork' in extraData. All transaction state transitions must be re-executed and state root verified.

All block header fields must be independently validated: parent hash, state root, transactions root, receipts root, difficulty (with bomb delay), gas limit, timestamp. PoW verification required for pre-Merge blocks.
Contract must verify caller's DAO token balance against mainDAO before transferring ether. Proportional distribution must be enforced. Transfer failure must throw exception.

Sender must verify recipient public key authenticity via signature chain before encapsulating. CSRNG must be used for ephemeral key generation. Ephemeral keys must be destroyed after protocol completion.
Ephemeral keys must be generated with CSRNG. Private ephemeral key must be securely stored until decryption. After key recovery, ephemeral keys must be securely destroyed for PFS.

If signerPubKey is provided, signature on public key R must be verified. If trustedPubKey is provided, full trust chain must be validated. Without signature verification, protocol is vulnerable to MITM.

Element indices must be bounds-checked. Context-specific size limits should be enforced. Proof generation must handle edge cases (empty lists returning zero hash). Progressive tree structure must provide equivalent collision resistance to fixed-capacity trees.
